# Agents SDK: own the runtime

[Course guide](../../docs/course-guide.md) · [Exercise](exercise.md) · [Worked solution](solution.md)

## 04 · Agents SDK: own the runtime — 25 min

**Outcome:** Rebuild the task with Agent, function_tool, and Runner; compare state and execution ownership.

> The SDK runs the loop inside our application; our application still owns its permissions and state strategy.

### Teaching beats

- 0–7: map Agent, function_tool, output_type, and Runner to the previous loop.
- 7–14: run a brief and a follow-up, inspect local run events.
- 14–19: demonstrate a failing function tool.
- 19–25: choose a runtime for two concrete deployment scenarios.

### Explain and show

- course/runtimes/sdk.py wraps the same ToolBox functions using function_tool, constructs Agent, and asks Runner.run_streamed to orchestrate the run.
- The application supplies deployment, tool code, storage decisions, identity, and approval enforcement. Runner provides the orchestration loop.
- The completed demo carries result.to_input_list() into the next turn. This local SDK history is not a managed API session or a sandbox.
- The SDK demo disables hosted tracing and records local results/events. Traces are useful diagnostics; they do not grade correctness.
- A shared tool contract and schema make comparison possible. Reusing a session object across unrelated runtimes is not part of that contract.

### Completed demo

Run from the repository root. Live commands make API requests; choose one prepared runtime rather than running every alternative in class.

```bash
uv run python -m course demo --runtime sdk --follow-up --output outputs/sdk
uv run python -m course demo --runtime sdk --failure read_paper --output outputs/sdk-failure
```

**Open:** [course/runtimes/sdk.py](../../course/runtimes/sdk.py) · [course/runtimes/responses.py](../../course/runtimes/responses.py) · [course/runtimes/managed.py](../../course/runtimes/managed.py) · [course/tools.py](../../course/tools.py)

### Exercise

- Choose a runtime for a hosted research worker that should retain progress between tasks. State one reason and one responsibility that remains yours.
- Choose a runtime for an existing application with its own user permissions and custom database. Explain how you would retain follow-up state.
- Run the failed read_paper demo. Check whether missing primary evidence is disclosed and secondary summaries are labeled.

### Expected solution

- The managed Agents API is a reasonable choice for the hosted worker when its access, retention, environment, and billing fit. The application still controls tool validation and authorization.
- The Agents SDK is a reasonable choice for an existing application with custom storage and permissions. Persist SDK-compatible history or use a supported SDK session strategy; the classroom demo keeps local history only. Responses is also defensible when explicit loop control is the priority.
- An unavailable PDF must not silently turn a CSV summary into primary-paper evidence. Inspect tool_calls, not_found, limitations, and citations; repair any unsupported claim.

**Checkpoint:** Find Agent, a function_tool, Runner.run_streamed, and the saved SDK history. Explain what the SDK replaced and what remains application code.

**Fallback:** Inspect sdk.py alongside the offline demo; use local events or a recorded SDK output to compare state. Do not claim Runner ran if the SDK live call was unavailable.
